title: Redbeak common definitions 0.1
description: Shared primitives for the Redbeak 0.1 contract. Constraints are expressed with `pattern` rather than `format` assertions so that TypeScript and Python validators accept and reject identically without format plugins.

schema_version.description: Redbeak contract version carried by every envelope payload.

sha256.description: Content hash, always prefixed so the algorithm is explicit.

sequence.description: Zero-based turn index within one case execution.

opaque_token.description: Bearer-equivalent capability string. Never logged, never persisted in evidence.

fact_name.description: Pre-agreed name of an observable fact. Names only; the contract never carries an expected value.

data_classification.description: Demo v0 is synthetic-only. Real customer data is prohibited until TaiwanEval's Pilot Data Handling Policy defines retention, deletion, access, incident, and subcontractor boundaries.

evaluation_private_property_names.description: Property names that must never cross the trust boundary into a customer environment. Exact names only: prefix matching would reject legitimate domain data such as a travel mock's `expected_arrival`. `path` is deliberately absent because it is a legitimate key in a file-system mock; BFCL's evaluator-private `path` must be excluded by explicit importer field mapping instead, which is what the field map already requires.

leak_free_object.description: An object of otherwise unconstrained shape that still cannot carry evaluation-private material at any depth. This is the runtime half of the data-boundary guarantee: because the orchestrator validates its own outgoing payloads, a wholesale copy of an upstream record that still carries `ground_truth` fails validation before it is ever sent, in both TypeScript and Python.

observation_request.description: Names of the facts the adapter should observe. It carries no expected values, rubrics, or thresholds; the evaluator alone decides whether an observed fact satisfies a hidden expected outcome.

execution_error.description: A failure that prevented the case from producing a judgeable answer. A target that answers *poorly* is NOT an error: that is a normal completed turn whose quality the evaluator judges, and routing it here would let customer-written adapter code drop its own weak results out of the denominator. A target that is *unreachable or crashed* is `target_unavailable`, which is attributable to the system under test rather than to Redbeak infrastructure.

stage.description: `target_unavailable` belongs to the system under test; every other value is a Redbeak-side or integration fault and must be reported separately from target results.

operational.description: Minimal operational metadata. Deliberately small: it must never become a side channel for scenario content, agent internals, or credentials.
